content:
I'm a Windows user and thought it would be nice to have Windows developer documentation, like the Ubuntu one. I spun up a VM so I could make sure I documented all the necessary steps.

- Install [MSYS2](https://www.msys2.org) and accept defaults
  - When the install finishes, in the console that opens type:
`pacman -Syu`
  - Reopen the console if it closes (MSYS2 MSYS), and continue to run the command until there are no more updates.
  - Install the ART dependencies:
`pacman -S mingw-w64-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-x86_64-gdb mingw-w64-x86_64-make mingw-w64-x86_64-pkg-config mingw-w64-x86_64-cmake mingw-w64-x86_64-ninja mingw-w64-x86_64-gtkmm3 mingw-w64-x86_64-lcms2 mingw-w64-x86_64-fftw mingw-w64-x86_64-exiv2 mingw-w64-x86_64-lensfun mingw-w64-x86_64-libiptcdata mingw-w64-x86_64-gtk3 mingw-w64-x86_64-mimalloc mingw-w64-x86_64-opencolorio mingw-w64-x86_64-libraw`
- Install [cmake](https://cmake.org/download/#latest)
- Install [Visual Studio Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/Download)
  - Open Visual Studio
  - Open the extensions marketplace (Ctrl+Shift+X) and install `C/C++ Extension Pack`
  - Choose File, Open Folder..., and choose the root ART folder
  - Choose to trust the authors
  - You should get a popup saying "Compiler kits may be present in these directories", with a list of directories from your MSYS2 installation. Choose the Yes option to set up the compiler kits. If the popup goes away you can open the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) and choose `CMake: Scan for Kits` to open it again.
  - Open the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) and choose `CMake: Set Launch/Debug Target`. First you'll be prompted to select a kit. Choose `CC xx.x.x x86_64-w64-mingw32 (mingw64)`, where xx.x.x is the version number of the compiler you have installed. Wait until VS is done configuring the project, then you will be prompted to choose a launch target. Choose `art (Install)`.
  - By default the debug configuration will be selected. If you'd like to build a different one, open the command palette and choose `CMake: Select Variant`.
  - In Visual Studio press Shift+F5 to start debugging.

The Rawtherapee's custom command: `/usr/bin/flatpak run --branch=stable --arch=x86_64 --command=gimp-3.0 --file-forwarding org.gimp.GIMP @@u %U @@` [discussion-comment discussion-comment:DC_kwDONWPV1M4A6DN4] Hi, try with a wrapper shell script, something like this: ```bash #!/bin/sh /usr/bin/flatpak run --branch=stable --arch=x86_64 --command=gimp-3.0 --file-forwarding org.gimp.GIMP "$1" ``` If you call the script e.g. `photogimp.sh`, then simply specify its path in the preferences (and make sure that the script is actually executable): HTH

As recent addition of Filmsim's, i tried the vkdt implementation of filmsim first and liked but the workflow wasnt for me and WB is a bit messed up. as coming from that to ART, it have been a pleasent ride but i cant ignore the absence of Halation and upscale feature in ART. 

As from my understanding, ART is using napari in background for filmsim's. Napari has halation and Grain. there's film grain i

[discussion-comment discussion-comment:DC_kwDONWPV1M4A6YYd]
Hi,

ART uses a LUT for the film simulations. This means that it can only apply "point-wise" functions, i.e. effects that look at a single pixel at a time. Both halation and grain are "spatial" operations, that need to look at a neighborhood of each pixel, and are not possible to implement with a LUT. That's why they are not available in the film simulations. 
But they exist in other forms in ART, specifically in "Local Editing -> Smoothing" (mode "Halation" for halation, and mode "Add noise" for grain). Grain is also available in "Special Effects", but that's a simple recipe that might not be to your liking. 
If you want more control, including support for multiple instances and masking, you can take a look at the Add noise mode of the smoothing tool. It won't be the same as filmsim, because the algorithm is very different, but it gives you a bit more flexibility than the simple film grain tool.

Hope this helps

Hi,
a quite unusual approach nowadays, reminds me of Unix (were rename is made with the mv command, as far as I remember). Works so far and feels quite practical, but I would suggest some improvements (in order of "importance" ;-)):

1. Change the menu name to "Rename/Move" to make this functionality clear to the "unsuspecting" user. (BTW, if you need/want support for the German language, I could be of help.)

2. Move the XMP file too, since this is part of the "bundle". (I tested on Linux. I didn't check if the Rename operation already does it. XnView MP has an interesting feature regarding sidecar files, as it includes JPEG and lets one define additional extensions.)

3. When first clicking on the folder selection for the move operation, use the current directory of the file browser (as is indicated by the "." on first use), not with some other folder. (I tested this on macOS, Windows and Linux, and it were totally different locations; opening the home folder in Linux was the most sensible of the three. ;-))

4. Related to point 3: The "Base directory:" is misleading, as it points to the last base directory, not the current (again, on Linux). This is shown in the "Preview" string, but this is not what I would expect. Didn't test it in RT.

Best

section_title: ART newbie: How to reuse the same mask I painted in one tool in one or more other tools?
content:
Hi all and please excuse my ignorance:

I painted a mask over a beautiful bird sitting on an branch.
I used some fine contrast to be applied only to this masked bird - it works as expected.

**My question:**

Now I want to reuse this same mask elsewhere ... but I don't see / find a way how to refer to it. How can I achieve the intended reuse?

**_NB:_** I used to use _darktable_ for years but find it's GUI and tools behaviour much less than comfortable. Thus I currently investigate **ART** .... having already left _RawTherapee_ behind due to the lack of advanced selective retouching options.

[discussion-comment discussion-comment:DC_kwDONWPV1M4A7gGl]
Hi, yes it's possible. You just have to give a name to the mask, and then it will appear in subsequent tools as a "Liked mask". "Subsequent" here means that the tool / region follows the one in which you originally defined the mask in the processing pipeline (the order is the same as you see on the screen, from top to bottom).

Here's a quick video that shows how to do it:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0abb23c-fb24-40ef-ad55-ad81ec94c5bc



[discussion-comment discussion-comment:DC_kwDONWPV1M4A7hf1]
Hi, 
you are right, you can only reuse masks in tools that appear later in the pipeline. This is not something that can be relaxed easily, and I have no plans of changing it in the near future, sorry. However, you can copy/paste a mask from a tool to another freely. The masks might not be identical (because the result of parametric masks depend on where they are applied in the pipeline), but should be close enough to give you a reasonable starting point.
If this is still not enough, I'm afraid ART is not the right tool, sorry.

HTH

section_title: Feature Request: Sony Alpha A7 V Raw Support
content:
## Feature Request: Sony Alpha A7 V Raw Support

### Summary
Request for support of Sony Alpha A7 V raw files (.ARW format) in ART.

### Camera Details
- **Camera model:** Sony Alpha A7 V
- **Raw format:** Lossless .ARW files
- **Status:** Currently not supported by ART

### Issue Description
The Sony Alpha A7 V is a recently released camera, and ART does not currently recognize or process its raw files. Support depends on LibRaw adding compatibility for this model.

When attempting to open lossless .ARW files, ART displays the embedded JPEG preview but exhibits critical issues in edit mode.

### Bugs Observed
1. **Aberrant tone curve behavior** – Tone curve adjustments produce incorrect tonal results and don't respond as expected
2. **Black borders on right and bottom edges** – Dark borders appear on the right side and bottom of the image, cutting off valid image data

### Expected Behavior
Once LibRaw releases an update with A7 V support, ART should be able to:
- Open and display Sony A7 V lossless .ARW files correctly
- Apply tone curves and edits without artifacts
- Process raw data without border clipping

### Additional Information
- This is a dependency on LibRaw's underlying raw decoding library
- Sample .ARW file: https://discuss.pixls.us/uploads/short-url/oqgf2RTjo7LNcUcpKtRWJvAOhLA.ARW
